task_statement:
Research question (as posed on 2026-08-08, in the area of structural roles and influence):
Cut-heavy shapers' roles travel better than drive-heavy ones.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.
- Units available to a study of this question (as recorded): n=24

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.

methodological_questions: Can role portability be tested with n=24 units?
How should cut-heavy versus drive-heavy profiles be defined from play-by-play?
What sample size and exposure are needed for a role-transfer comparison?
How should confounding by usage, lineup and team context be controlled?

historical_evidence.finding: Coverage > accumulation confirmatory test (T_cov). Recorded result: an adequately powered null. Prereg-recorded run gave +0.67 pts/100, p=0.176; the later run gave beta=+0.42 pts/100, p=0.595, with MDE80=2.19 pts/100 across 72 team-seasons. Limitations recorded: low power, large MDE, drift/nonstationarity, sample size power.

Coverage feasibility gate, not an outcome test. 90 team-seasons with 420,993 possessions; 72 team-seasons met the >=200 possession threshold in both strata. Recorded gate checks: |rho(COVERED,TALENT)|=0.042, aux R2=0.203, rho(TALENT,PPP)=+0.027. Beta was not computed. Validation status recorded as NOT_RECORDED.

Absence validation. V1 (absence moves association structure) was partly supported: 16/23 above own-null p95, binomial p=2.67e-16, and V1(b) +0.142 CI [+0.103, +0.187] confirmed in [prior work]. V2a (rho=+0.288, p=0.077, CI crosses 0) and V2b (partial +0.253, p=0.115) failed. Limitation recorded: small sample.

Portability confirmatory T1 on a mover's displacement signature across franchises versus profile-matched decoys: median Delta=+0.0557, perm p=0.0050, 173/294 positive, sign p=2.87e-3. This concerns franchise portability of movers' signatures, not cut-heavy versus drive-heavy role classes. Risk recorded: placebo dependence.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Testing whether lineups covering all three core roles outscore on a per-possession net basis after controlling for role counts and talent
failed_approaches.why: Adequately powered null result with a large MDE (2.19 pts/100 at 72 team-seasons). Recorded limitation: low power with large MDE. A design with 24 units would have a larger MDE, so a null would not be informative.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Predicting the magnitude of association-structure change under real player absence using a LOO simulation (V2a/V2b)
failed_approaches.why: Both V2 checks failed: CIs cross zero (V2a CI [-0.244, +0.667]; V2b CI [-0.262, +0.615]). Recorded limitation: small sample.

evidence_establishes: The project's existing records show that role-coverage and related structure tests in this data family were run at 72-90 team-seasons, not at 24 units, and that the power to detect effects of about 2 pts/100 was limited even at that scale.
Historical tests of this family relied on team-season units and talent/count controls, so a cut-heavy versus drive-heavy comparison would need comparable controls.

Portability-style tests in this project ([prior work]) were run as cross-franchise comparisons against matched decoys, which suggests a possible template, but [prior work]'s findings do not address role classes.
evidence_does_not_establish: No retrieved record tests cut-heavy versus drive-heavy role portability.
No retrieved record defines or validates a cut-heavy or drive-heavy classification from play-by-play.
No retrieved record gives an effect size or direction for role portability by shaper type.
Nothing retrieved shows that n=24 units can detect a role-portability difference.
Retrieval returned no record for the 2025-26 playoffs data version or the 24-unit configuration.
own_inferences: At 24 units, the MDE would be well above the 2.19 pts/100 MDE of FAM:[prior work], so a null would be uninformative and a positive result would be fragile.
Without a validated classifier of cut-heavy versus drive-heavy profiles, any 'portability' measure would be partly a function of the classification choice.
The question as posed compares two role types and makes a directional claim ('travel better'), but 'travel' is not operationalised in any retrieved record.
The 2022-23 to 2025-26 seasons span changes in play style and rotation, so pooling them risks drift that would masquerade as role effects.
uncertainties: The retrieval returned only four records, none on this exact question. Relevant earlier work may exist but was not returned.
The n=24 unit definition is not described (team-seasons, players, or lineups?).
The status 'supported' for SF-[prior work] reflects a feasibility gate, not a substantive hypothesis test.
Validation status for SF-[prior work] is recorded as NOT_RECORDED.
The 2025-26 regular season and playoffs are partial before 2026-04-13 and 2026-06-21, so the data version matters.

historical_effect.explanation: The historical records show that comparable role-structure tests on this data family were underpowered or null at 72-90 team-seasons, and that a small-sample V2 prediction failed. Together these shifted the decision from a plain feasibility check to not proceeding with the question as posed at n=24 units. The retrieved records do not test the specific hypothesis, so this is a judgement from their power and limitation records.

blocking_constraints.text: 24 units give little power to detect a per-possession or portability effect of the size that earlier team-season tests could not resolve (MDE of about 2.2 pts/100 at 72 team-seasons).
No validated cut-heavy versus drive-heavy classification exists in the retrieved records; the classification must be defined and its reliability shown before any portability test.
Play-type labels and points come from the same play-by-play used for the outcome, so classification and outcome may not be independent.

prior_work.summary: No retrieved record tests whether cut-heavy shaper roles travel better than drive-heavy roles. The nearest records are a null coverage test ([prior work]), a feasibility gate (SF-[prior work]), an absence-validation study with failed V2 checks ([prior work]), and a cross-franchise portability test on a different construct ([prior work]). They inform power, controls and possible design templates but do not answer the question.

risks.text: With n=24 units, the MDE will exceed the roughly 2.2 pts/100 MDE of prior team-season tests; a null is uninformative and a positive result is likely inflated.
The cut-heavy versus drive-heavy profile and the 'travel' measure are undefined; reliability and split-half stability are unknown.
Usage, lineup, team talent and team context may drive both role type and transfer outcomes; [prior work] needed talent and count controls for this reason.
Play-type classification and points both come from play-by-play, so a shared derivation could create spurious association.
Pooling 2022-23 to 2025-26 and partial 2025-26 data mixes seasons with different play styles, and [prior work] recorded drift as a risk.
[prior work] recorded placebo dependence on profile-matched decoys; any role-portability test would need decoy or placebo controls and their sensitivity checked.
Multiple cut-heavy/drive-heavy thresholds or transfer definitions would inflate false positives unless fixed in advance.

design.estimand: Not estimable as posed. Minimum viable estimand: difference in a pre-registered, validated portability score between cut-heavy and drive-heavy shaper roles, adjusted for usage, lineup and team talent.
design.unit: Not fixed by retrieval. Possession-level or player-season units with team-season clustering would be needed; team-season units alone are insufficient at n=24.
design.sample: The available n=24 units are insufficient. The minimum viable test requires more units (e.g., all team-seasons from 2022-23 to 2025-26, about 120 team-seasons, or player-seasons) and a classification validated on held-out seasons.
design.power: Not computed. Prior team-season tests in this data family had an MDE of about 2.2 pts/100 at 72 team-seasons; a pre-registered power calculation must be done for the chosen unit and effect size before any run.
design.controls: Usage, lineup composition, team talent, and season/drift fixed effects; decoy-matched or profile-matched placebo comparisons as in [prior work]; clustering by team and franchise.
design.falsification: Pre-register that a portability advantage for cut-heavy roles should disappear under profile-matched decoys and should not appear for drive-heavy roles in a placebo classification.
design.multiplicity: Fix one cut-heavy/drive-heavy threshold and one portability score in advance; any alternatives are exploratory and reported as such.
design.decision_rule: Support requires a pre-specified positive difference whose CI excludes zero after clustering, surviving decoy placebo and the season-holdout check. Otherwise report as null with MDE, or untestable if the classification fails its reliability check.
design.data_version: Only complete seasons (2022-23, 2023-24, 2024-25 regular season and playoffs, and 2025-26 regular season after 2026-04-13 and playoffs after 2026-06-21). Partial 2025-26 data excluded. Record the data snapshot date.
